links.outcome: LLM discharge summary completeness and structural accuracy against original notes, highlighted vs unhighlighted input
links.effect: H-summaries 96% completeness vs 88% for U-summaries (P=.01); improper headers 4 vs 30 (P=.03); misplaced information 2 vs 8; false information items 2 vs 3.
links.quote: On average, the completeness of the U-summaries was 88% (SD 6%), while the completeness of the H-summaries was 96% (SD 4%), which was 8% higher.

unlisted_practices: Highlighting key information in input notes (interface terminology) before LLM summarization to improve summary accuracy
Iterative prompt engineering for structured summaries

links.outcome: AI summary omissions and erroneous information
links.effect: Completeness was 96% vs 88%; erroneous information 2 vs 3; misplaced information 2 vs 8 for H-summaries vs U-summaries.
links.quote: Moreover, H-summaries demonstrated better correctness than U-summaries, with fewer instances of erroneous information (2 vs 3 errors, respectively).

unlisted_practices: Highlighting detailed information in discharge notes using an interface terminology before LLM summarization.
Prompt engineering to produce short structured EHR note summaries.

links.outcome: factual errors in LLM-generated discharge note summaries
links.effect: 3 false information items in unhighlighted summaries and 2 in highlighted summaries (0.38% vs 0.23% of items)
links.quote: In our analysis, we identified 3 instances of false information in U-summaries.
